name: MileMath — mileage reimbursement computed pages (rate x distance x year)
oneLiner: Per-distance computed pages ('350 miles at the 2026 IRS rate = $266') exploiting the rare July 1, 2026 mid-year rate change that made every competitor's number wrong overnight.
keywordFamily: '[N] miles mileage reimbursement 2026', 'how much is [N] miles at 72.5 cents', '[state] mileage reimbursement rate 2026', medical/charity/military rate variants — distances log-scaled 1-5,000 x 4 rate types x year + 50 state pages ≈ 1,200-1,800 pages.
demandEvidence: Search verified: IRS set 2026 business rate at 72.5¢ then issued a rare mid-year increase to 76¢ effective July 1, 2026 (irs.gov newsroom) — two rate events in one year; commercial demand proven by Ramp, Brex, Zoho, Everlance all maintaining calculator pages for these terms.
competition: Fintech authorities own 'mileage reimbursement calculator' head terms; the per-distance computed long tail is classic unbuilt KGR/zero-volume territory (same shape datesum already won); state-rate pages are semi-built by HR blogs with stale numbers.
monetization: Business/finance AdSense — the digest's $30-60 finance RPM band with high-CPC expense-management advertisers (Ramp/Brex/Everlance are literally the bidders); highest-RPM idea of the 8.
successCase: datesum.com itself (597 per-quantity computed pages, indexed in 10 days, click day 8) plus inchcalculator.com (5.26M visits/mo on unit-quantity pages) — identical page shape, moved into the finance vertical.
cleverTwist: Freshness exploit with real substance: every page shows a Jan-Jun 2026 (72.5¢) vs Jul-Dec 2026 (76¢) split table while stale competitor pages show one wrong number — the 'updated July 2026' dateModified reflects a genuine data change, exactly the kind the Dec 2025 core update rewards while punishing date-bumpers. 40-60-word answer-first block + split table targets snippets on every calculation query; each new IRS announcement (annual + any mid-year) is a recurring refresh wave competitors sleep through.
buildNotes: Data: IRS newsroom rates + GSA POV rates + state-published rates (all free, official). Pure arithmetic templates; smallest build of the 8 (~3 days for wave 1). Tricky: stay strictly 'rate x distance = $' with official citations — zero deduction/tax advice (YMYL guardrail keeps AdSense approval clean).
risk: Finance-adjacent means stricter AdSense content scrutiny (mitigate: factual arithmetic only); individual query volumes are tiny so the family pays in aggregate; a fintech incumbent could programmatically expand downward, though their content teams have ignored this long tail for years.

verify.confidence: high on facts (every data claim independently verified live); medium on demand — exact per-distance query volume is unproven and the closest existing query family is already occupied
verify.findings: All factual claims verified: IRS Notice 2026-10 set 72.5¢, and the rare mid-year increase to 76¢ effective July 1, 2026 is real (announced ~July 10–13; Forbes/JofA/SHRM/Littler). Staleness confirmed live: Ramp's calculator still shows 72.5¢-only, no split, 4 days post-announcement. But competition is understated: saving.org's programmatic per-rate pages rank #1 for "[N] miles at 72.5 cents" and it already built its 76¢ page; state pages are held by Ramp/Brex programmatic pages plus official state agencies, not stale HR blogs. Per-distance-by-year queries ("350 miles mileage reimbursement 2026") show no exact-answer page. inchcalculator 5.26M visits/mo confirmed (Semrush); datesum is real but has 1 click and $0 revenue so far.
verify.improvedTwist: Key every page to distance × year × purpose ("350 miles mileage reimbursement 2026") — a URL/query family saving.org's rate-keyed pages (/mileage/725) structurally cannot match — and make the Jan–Jun 72.5¢ vs Jul–Dec 76¢ split table the answer block, since no ranking page answers "which half of the year applies". Deprioritize the "[N] miles at [X] cents" family (saving.org entrenched, already updated to 76¢) and the 50-state family (Ramp/Brex + official state sites own it); keep states only as thin citation hubs. Institutionalize the refresh wave: ship 2027 pages within hours of the IRS's mid-December notice, when every competitor's 2026 pages go stale simultaneously.

Next closure: Labor Day, in 46 days') so dateModified changes daily with genuinely changing computed values — legitimate freshness the Dec 2025 update rewards. Client-side JS handles 'open right now' timezone logic. ~500 pages. Tricky: unscheduled closures (national mourning days) need a same-day manual hotfix path via CI.

competition: Single-page calculators and scattered blog posts; nobody has shipped the full model-x-GPU programmatic matrix. Head term 'LLM VRAM calculator' is now contested — the play is the long-tail leaves ('run qwen3 32b on 16gb vram') which are KGR/zero-volume territory.
monetization: AdSense in the digest's SaaS/software band ($30-65 RPM, US dev-heavy traffic — best RPM class available to a utility site); optional Amazon Associates GPU/RAM links later (low % but $500+ AOV).
successCase: Omni Calculator: 3,700 single-question calculator pages, 23-30M visits/mo, AdSense (digest); plus the 2025-26 indie VRAM sites above already ranking proves a fresh domain wins this SERP.

buildNotes: Data: HuggingFace model config API (free) for params/architecture + hand-compiled static GPU/Apple-Silicon spec table (~40 rows). Formula-driven pages, WebApplication + BreadcrumbList schema, hub-spoke prebuilt. ~4-5 days. Tricky: quantization overhead constants must match llama.cpp/GGUF reality or the dev audience will dismiss it — validate against a dozen known-good community benchmarks before launch.

The defensible pivot is a measured-throughput database: real tok/s benchmarks per model-quant-hardware combo aggregated from community submissions (r/LocalLLaMA, llama.cpp discussions) — data that cannot be computed client-side, which every incumbent lacks. Keep the Bing/IndexNow + GPTBot-open GEO play, but as table stakes (apxml already gets AI-cited), not a moat. keywordFamily: '[model] charging time 20-80 [7kW/11kW/50kW/150kW]', '[model] cost to charge at home in [state]', DE 'Ladezeit [model] 11 kW', NL 'laadtijd [model]' — ~400 models x 4-5 charger tiers ≈ 1,800 EN pages + ~800 DE/NL pages in a second wave.
demandEvidence: Search verified: English SERP is generic single calculators (evchargecal.com, blinkcharging, chargemath — only 22 vehicles deep); gaps digest calls the per-model long tail 'mostly unbuilt' (electricniverse ~200 thin pages). German check: solo-run tessybase.de ranks top for 'Tesla Model Y Ladezeit' and covers ONLY Tesla — per-model demand proven in DE with 399 models unserved.
competition: chargemath (22 vehicles), electricniverse/electricvehiclegeek (thin recent indies), OEM pages and utility blogs (enbw) that answer only their own models. No full-matrix player in any language.
monetization: AdSense auto niche (mid-tier RPM) + the real layer: Amazon Associates home/portable EV chargers ($200-600 AOV, direct purchase intent on every page) — amazon.de/amazon.com via Payoneer US receiving account per digest payment rails.
successCase: tessybase.de — a solo per-model Ladezeit site ranking #1 in Germany proves the exact page format wins; inchcalculator.com (5.26M visits/mo on unit-quantity pages, digest) proves the scale ceiling.
cleverTwist: Non-English SERP arbitrage (the vecka.nu lesson from the digest applied to a non-date niche): identical dataset, translated templates, into DE/NL/Nordic SERPs that are 2+ years behind English. Plus snippet capture: comparison tables win calculation queries, and DC fast-charge answers computed from real charge curves (not linear math) give every page a defensibly unique number that generic calculators get wrong — state that difference on-page.
buildNotes: Data: open-ev-data-dataset on GitHub (free, community JSON incl. battery capacity and DC charge curves — verified) + EIA state electricity rates API (free) for cost pages. Deterministic formula pages, WebApplication schema, model hubs with sibling links. ~5-6 days for EN wave. Tricky: do NOT scrape ev-database.org (licensed data — they sell API access); use open-ev-data + own compilation.
risk: Auto-niche AdSense RPM is mid-tier not finance-tier; open-ev-data coverage gaps for obscure models mean hand-filling ~50 rows; DE/NL editions need native-quality translation review or they'll read as machine output.

verify.findings: Live SERPs killed the core premise. EN: evadept.com already has per-model charging-time calculators across 15+ brands with charger tiers/windows; costtocharge.com is the exact per-model x per-state home-cost matrix (vehicles/{make}/{model} + states/{state}, ZIP-linked rates, monthly refresh). DE: tessybase.de is real, Tesla-only, ranks — but praxis-elektroauto.de (multi-brand Ladezeiten pages), amperepoint, mobilityhouse also rank; not a 2-years-behind SERP. NL: ANWB (major brand) plus multiple installers hold per-model laadtijd queries. Data: open-ev-data-dataset verified — CDLA-Permissive-2.0, 1,189 vehicles/65 makes, battery net kWh + AC/DC max power present, but ZERO records contain charge curves, gutting the 'real charge curve' differentiator. EIA API free, state-level prices confirmed.
verify.improvedTwist: The only surviving edge: hand-compile actual DC charge curves for the top ~100 models (Fastned/P3/InsideEVs published test curves), since no free dataset ships them and every ranking calculator uses linear math — make measured 10-80/20-80 minutes the on-page hook. Target DE/NL only at ultra-granular windows ('Ladezeit [model] 20-80 11 kW') that multi-brand incumbents answer only generically, and skip the EN cost-to-charge family entirely — costtocharge.com already owns it.

name: WattCost — appliance running-cost pages x state electricity rates
oneLiner: "How much does it cost to run a [appliance] in [state]" pages powered by EIA's monthly state price data — every page's dollar figures are unique and refresh monthly.
keywordFamily: "cost to run a [appliance] per hour/month" (120 appliance hubs: space heater, pool pump, hot tub, window AC, dehumidifier, gaming PC, grow tent...) x "[state]" for the top 25 appliances (25 x 51 = 1,275) ≈ 1,400 pages phase 1.
demandEvidence: Search-verified today for "cost to run space heater": perchenergy.com, energysage.com, learnmetrics.com, wattmath.fyi, calcbee.com, pickhvac.com all farm the appliance head terms — but none has the appliance x state matrix; state-level long tail is thin forum/blog results.
competition: EnergySage is strong on head terms; the rest of the verified SERP is indie sites (wattmath.fyi is a fresh solo site ranking now, learnmetrics is a classic indie) — the weak-SERP gate passes at appliance x state level, which nobody has built.
monetization: AdSense home/energy ($10-25 RPM, energy bills are money-adjacent-not-advice) + Amazon affiliate on smart plugs/energy monitors/efficient heaters ($20-80 items with natural in-context placement).
successCase: ecocostsavings.com and learnmetrics.com — indie one-person appliance-energy sites that ranked for years on this template; wattmath.fyi verified today as a brand-new indie already on page 1 for the space-heater query.
cleverTwist: EIA's free monthly state electricity-price API makes freshness structural: every page's core numbers ($/hr, $/mo in that state) genuinely change monthly — legitimate dateModified bumps + "July 2026 rates" in titles that the Dec 2025 update can't discount, and CA-vs-LA rate spreads (3x) make each state page's synthesis genuinely distinct (the ≥30-40% uniqueness bar). Seasonality timing per digest's Q4 RPM multiplier (1.35x): launch heating appliances in September, cooling in April, so pages peak with both query volume and ad rates.
buildNotes: Data: EIA open API (free, no key cost) + a 120-row appliance wattage table compiled from manufacturer spec sheets (use honest wattage RANGES, not fake precision). ~1,400 pages; 4 days plus a monthly GitHub Action rebuild. Interactive kWh-rate calculator on every page for AIO resistance.
risk: Head terms partially AIO-absorbed already (generic "$0.26/hr" answers); the state-specific numbers and calculator are the moat. Electricity pricing is politically topical — stay strictly descriptive, never advise switching providers (keeps it out of YMYL and off regulators' radar).

verify.confidence: high on the core kill finding (direct SERP + on-site evidence that the claimed unclaimed niche is already occupied); medium on success-case checks, one of which was bot-walled
verify.findings: Live SERPs kill the moat claim: priceofelectricity.com already runs the exact play — EIA-sourced appliance x state x city pages ("modeled from the April 2026 EIA state average", dataset updated July 7 2026, calculators, methodology, downloadable data) — ranking page 1 for "pool pump Florida" and surfacing for "space heater Ohio". State long-tail SERPs are not thin: energy retailers (Perch, Santanna, Direct Energy, BKV) publish state-rate content and local dealers own "hot tub in Texas"; head terms carry Bob Vila, Family Handyman, HomeGuide, Angi, with AI answers already giving per-state cents/hr. EIA API verified free (free key, monthly state retail prices). Success cases shaky: wattmath.fyi exists but never appeared in my SERPs; ecocostsavings.com bot-walled; learnmetrics absent (learnmetering ranked instead).
verify.improvedTwist: Don't clone the state matrix — priceofelectricity.com owns it with the same EIA feed. If salvaging: (1) cover appliances it and the retailers ignore (grow tent, gaming PC, 3D printer, kegerator, aquarium) with honest duty-cycle ranges; (2) go one level deeper than state averages via OpenEI's free Utility Rate Database — "cost to run X on FPL / ConEd / PG&E TOU rates" — utility- and time-of-use-level numbers that nobody in the verified SERPs computes; (3) add seasonal load modeling (hot tub heating in TX winter vs MN) so figures differ from the generic $/hr answers AI overviews already give. Utility-level tariff granularity is the only remaining data moat.

name: NomadThreshold — nomad-visa income requirements, computed per household
oneLiner: Per-country x household-size pages that compute the actual income threshold ('Spain nomad visa income for a family of 4 in 2026') from each country's statutory formula, plus a do-I-qualify checker.
keywordFamily: '[country] digital nomad visa income requirement 2026', '[country] nomad visa income family of [N]', 'do I qualify for [country] nomad visa on $[X]/month' — ~60 countries x household sizes 1-5 + comparison hub ≈ 400-600 pages (small, dense cluster).
demandEvidence: Search verified head-term demand: immigrantinvest (55 visas), freelancermap, visahq, globalcitizensolutions all maintain 2026 country lists; thresholds confirmed moving annually (Portugal €3,680/mo 2026, Spain 200% of SMI, Romania 3x average salary, +25-75% per dependent) — annual movement is the wedge.
competition: Authority list-pages own '[country] digital nomad visa' heads — do not fight there. The computed per-household pages and interactive qualify-checker are unbuilt; list articles state single-applicant numbers only and go stale mid-year.
monetization: Best affiliate stack of the 8: NordVPN (Impact 40%, $1.87 EPC — digest's top software EPC), Airalo eSIM (Impact 10-12%), nomad insurance via Impact/CJ, over travel AdSense ($12-25 RPM). All networks pay China via Payoneer/bank per digest.
successCase: Digest: Payscale (2.9M organic visits/mo) and Salary.com (1.35M/mo) prove programmatic threshold/salary page families rank and carry finance-adjacent RPMs.
cleverTwist: Thresholds are formulas, not facts — (multiple of minimum wage or average salary) + (% per dependent) — so every page renders a computed household table no list article has: unique-data column satisfied, and tables win featured snippets on calculation queries. Annual threshold resets make current-year-in-title freshness legitimate (37-640% CTR lift class per digest), with per-page citations to official immigration sources for the +30-40% GEO/AI-citation lift.
buildNotes: Dataset: ~60 rows hand-compiled by the agent from official immigration ministry pages (free), each row = base formula + dependent uplift + source URL + last-verified date. Smallest honest build of the 8 (~3-4 days). Tricky: strictly eligibility arithmetic with official citations — no application advice, no tax guidance (YMYL guardrail).
risk: YMYL-adjacent (visas + income) so editorial discipline matters; 60 countries need re-verification ~2x/year; an authority (VisaHQ) could add household tables — moat is freshness cadence, not data secrecy.

verify.confidence: high (live SERPs directly falsify the core "unbuilt" claim; success-case numbers falsified by third-party traffic tools)
verify.findings: SERPs are not thin: "Spain DNV income 2026" and "family of 4" queries return dedicated, 2026-updated income pages from Citizen Remote, Global Citizen Solutions, Jobbatical ("€2,849 Income Guide"), law firms (NIM Extranjería shows a computed per-dependent SMI table), plus official gov pages. The claimed wedge is already built: Nomads Embassy runs free per-country eligibility checkers (50+ visas), VisaHQ/Travel Off Path/Nomad Advisers have income-based checkers, and europevisacheck.com already has programmatic per-country /family pages (Croatia example, family-of-4 math included). Data source claim holds: statutory formulas are real, free, official (BOE, exteriores.gob.es; Croatia 2.5x avg salary +10%/dependent). Success case inflated: Payscale ~433K organic (Ahrefs) / ~900K (Semrush), not 2.9M; Salary.com ~897K, not 1.35M.
verify.improvedTwist: Static household tables and qualify-checkers are commoditized; the only contestable asset is update speed on annual formula resets. If pursued at all, reposition as a threshold-change tracker: monitor the statutory inputs (minimum-wage/average-salary decrees), publish diffs within days ("Croatia raised its nomad-visa income to €3,622/mo in March 2026 — here's the new family math"), keep a per-country changelog with official citations, and offer email alerts plus an embeddable/citable data widget so authority sites link to it. That targets spike-time news queries incumbents update slowly, rather than evergreen pages they already own.

name: FobBattery — key fob battery fitment lookup
oneLiner: Indexable per-URL pages answering "what battery does my [year make model] key fob take" — competitors hide the same data behind non-indexable dropdown widgets.
keywordFamily: "[year-range] [make] [model] key fob battery" (e.g., "2017-2022 honda cr-v key fob battery") — ~40 makes x 15 models x grouped year-ranges ≈ 3,500-4,500 pages, plus per-battery hub pages (CR2032, CR2450, CR1616...).
demandEvidence: Search-verified today: dedicated finder sites exist and rank (batterydetective.com, microbattery.com/key-fob-battery-finder, keylessentryremotefob.com, starstruckllc.com covering only 295 models) — demand proven by the count of sites built to serve it; Energizer publishes an official key-fob replacement PDF guide, confirming mass consumer demand.
competition: The verified competitors are almost all dropdown-widget finders — their data is NOT crawlable as one-URL-per-vehicle pages. Remaining SERP is YouTube videos and forum threads. This is the same widget-vs-pages gap wipersizechart.com exploited for wiper sizes.
monetization: Amazon Associates automotive (~4.5%) on CR2032 2-packs, fob shells, and trim tools — tiny basket but very high purchase intent — via Payoneer US receiving account; AdSense auto vertical on top. Later: adjacent fitment families (cabin air filter, wiper size) on the same domain.
successCase: wipersizechart.com — explicitly an Amazon Associates fitment site ranking for per-vehicle wiper queries (from research digest's gaps section); identical template+dataset shape.
cleverTwist: SERP-gap exploitation: turning widget-locked data into indexable static URLs, where the digest notes an internal link from an indexed page beats any sitemap entry — hub (make) → spoke (model) → leaf (year-range) with bidirectional links. Each page's unique-data columns: battery type, battery COUNT (many fobs take two), tool needed, smart-key vs flip-key variant note — conditional sections when trims differ. Answer-first "Takes one CR2032" block feeds snippets and PAA.
buildNotes: Data: compiled from Energizer/Duracell public cross-reference guides + owner's-manual specs (free). The compile is the real work — AI agent extracts, then spot-verify top-100-traffic models. ~4,000 pages in year-range groups to keep per-page uniqueness; 5-6 days. New model years each fall = natural freshness.
risk: Fitment accuracy: trim/keyless-entry variants within one model year can differ — wrong answers burn trust fast; mitigate with variant call-out boxes. Amazon's low commission means AdSense must carry half the load.

verify.confidence: high — three live SERPs plus direct fetches all point the same direction; the idea's core gap claim was directly falsified by named URLs
verify.findings: Live SERPs for 2019 CR-V, 2018 Camry, and F-150 fob-battery queries show the "widget-locked data" gap does not exist: batterypete.com, Walmart/rometechcases, Amazon per-vehicle battery SKUs, crvguide.com, hyundainclub.com, and keylessentryremotefob.com (which the idea mislabeled a dropdown site — it has crawlable per-year URLs like /toyota/camry/2018-toyota-camry/) already rank with indexable one-URL-per-vehicle pages. Energizer's free PDF is real but covers only 2012–2019, leaving newer years to manual compilation; F-150 fobs alone span CR2032/2xCR2025/CR2450, confirming the accuracy risk. wipersizechart.com success case is genuine (Amazon Associates, updated June 2026). One-word "CR2032" answers are maximal AI-Overview/zero-click bait, and a ~$5 battery at 4.5% pays ~$0.20/order.
verify.improvedTwist: Drop the "first indexable pages" premise — it's false. The only defensible wedge is variant disambiguation the incumbents skip: pages keyed to FCC ID (printed on every fob) rather than year/make/model, with battery count, fob-opening steps, tool needed, and smart-key vs flip-key call-outs — the long tail Amazon listings and dealer blogs don't structure. Even then, AI Overviews answering "CR2032" in-SERP cap the ceiling; treat it as a low-priority add-on family to an existing fitment domain, not a standalone build.

name: TokenLength — tokens-to-words converter family
oneLiner: Per-quantity conversion pages ('how many words is 8,000 tokens?') powered by real client-side tokenizers instead of the 0.75 rule of thumb everyone else uses.
keywordFamily: 'how many words is [N] tokens', '[N] tokens to words/pages/characters', 'how many tokens in [N] words', 'does [N] words fit in [model] context window', '128k context in pages' — N log-scaled 100→2M x 4 conversion directions + per-model context-window pages ≈ 800-1,000 pages.
demandEvidence: Exact-match indie pages already rank: oreateai.com has a dedicated '2000 tokens to words' page, nerdytools.com, wordcountertool.net, unitconverterzone.com run words-to-tokens sections, 101calculators.com (verified via search) — demand exists and the current occupants are bottom-tier.
competition: gptforwork.com tokenizer (semi-authority) owns the tool head term; everything else is low-authority pages hard-coding the 0.75 words/token ratio. No one runs real per-model tokenizers or covers the per-quantity long tail systematically.
monetization: AdSense SaaS/dev band ($30-65 RPM per digest) — audience is developers and content ops estimating API costs and context fits.
successCase: Calculator.net/unitconverters.net (Maple Tech): founder publicly said AdSense income passed his salary on unit-conversion pages (digest) — tokens are the newest 'unit', and the converter family shape is identical.
cleverTwist: Unique-data moat + CTR mechanics: bundle js-tiktoken client-side so every page shows a measured 5-model comparison table (GPT-4o/Claude/Gemini/Llama/DeepSeek tokenizers) — data no ratio-based competitor has and exactly the table format that wins featured snippets on calculation queries. Question-word titles (+14.1% CTR per Backlinko), keyword-in-URL (+45%), 40-60-word answer-first block feeding snippet, PAA, and AI-citation simultaneously.
buildNotes: js-tiktoken (MIT, free) + approximation factors for non-open tokenizers; precompute per-N tables at build time so pages work without JS; paste-your-text live tool on every page. ~3-4 days, ~800 pages. Tricky: lazy-load the tokenizer bundle to stay under the 150kb JS budget.
risk: Each query is near-zero individual volume — the family only pays in aggregate (datesum-style); AI Overviews can answer the ratio question inline, mitigated by the interactive tool and per-model measured tables.

verify.findings: SERPs confirmed thin: "how many words is 8000 tokens" ranks a crypto Q&A farm (btcc.com), X posts, and off-topic blogs; "2000 tokens to words" ranks the cited oreateai.com page plus generic OpenAI docs — no big brands on per-quantity queries. js-tiktoken verified: MIT, free, 5.76M weekly downloads, but OpenAI encodings only — Claude/Gemini tokenizers are not public, so the "measured 5-model table" is overclaimed. Success case verified on Google's own publisher-story page (Huiming Gu/Maple Tech: ad revenue passed salary, quit job). Dents: 4+ recent programmatic copycats already in the niche (howmanytokens.app, llmcalcs.com, calctrail, convertools), and every test query was fully answerable inline — peak AI Overview absorption risk. Viable, not strong.
verify.improvedTwist: Honest 5-model table: live client-side measurement for GPT-4o/GPT-4 via js-tiktoken (o200k/cl100k) plus Llama 3 and DeepSeek via their public HuggingFace tokenizer.json (transformers.js, lazy-loaded); for Claude and Gemini, precompute real ratios at build time using Anthropic's free count_tokens API and Gemini's free countTokens API on a reference corpus, labeled "API-measured" — still data no ratio-based competitor has, and precomputed per-N tables keep pages JS-free for snippets. Differentiate into the less-colonized, less-AIO-absorbable "does [N] words fit in [model] context window" family as the primary wedge rather than plain conversion.
